title: ALLAH
bullets: NAME
Allah is the Arabic name Muslims use for the one true God: the Creator worshipped by Ibrahim (Abraham), Ishaq (Isaac), Musa (Moses), Isa (Jesus), and Prophet Muhammad.
ARABIC
Arabic ilāh means “a god” or “deity.” Allah refers to God, the One worthy of worship. It is not a separate “Muslim god”; Arabic-speaking Christians also use Allah for God.
QUR'AN
Allah says: “Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me.” (Qur’an 20:14)
ONE
Surah al-Ikhlāṣ begins: “Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.” (Qur’an 112:1–2)
source: Qur’an 20:14; 112:1–4. Arabic usage and standard Arabic lexicography.

title: HOW TO USE THIS DECK
bullets: This is a Hanafi study aid, not a substitute for your imam.
Arabic is intentionally large so it can be studied and copied.

Red marks fard/wajib/prohibition; green Sunnah/duʿā; gold Qur'an/Allah emphasis; blue timing/sequence; purple voluntary salah; orange special occasions; teal travel/illness/danger; maroon death/janazah.
If your imam corrects a card, record the card number and exact correction so the deck can be revised cleanly.

title: WHAT IS THE HANAFI SCHOOL?
bullets: HANAFI
One of the four major Sunni schools of Islamic law, or madhhabs.
ORIGIN
It traces its legal tradition to Imam Abu Hanifa and was developed and transmitted especially through his students Abu Yusuf and Muhammad al-Shaybani.
MADHHAB
A madhhab is not a separate religion or sect. It is a disciplined method for understanding and applying Islamic law.
SOURCES
Hanafi jurists reason from the Qur'an, Sunnah, scholarly consensus, analogy, and other recognized legal principles.
PRACTICE
Hanafi fiqh covers worship and daily life, including salah, purification, fasting, marriage, business, travel, and many other matters.
THIS DECK
This deck follows Hanafi fiqh. When an important difference exists within the Hanafi school, or a major difference from another school matters, the card should say so.
note: Different Sunni madhhabs share the Qur'an and the Prophet's Sunnah while sometimes reaching different rulings on details of law.
source: Historical overview: Encyclopaedia Iranica, “Abu Hanifa”; standard histories of the Hanafi school.

title: SHAHADA
arabic: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
translit: Ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa ashhadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh.
meaning: I testify that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

title: WHEN YOU WAKE
arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
translit: Al-ḥamdu lillāhi alladhī aḥyānā baʿda mā amātanā wa ilayhi n-nushūr.
meaning: All praise is for Allah, who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the resurrection.

title: BEFORE ENTERING THE TOILET
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبُثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ
translit: Allāhumma innī aʿūdhu bika mina l-khubuthi wa-l-khabāʾith.
meaning: O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female devils.
bullets: Say the duʿā before entering.
Enter with the left foot first.
source: Sahih al-Bukhari 142; Sahih Muslim 375. Left-foot entry is established etiquette.

title: AFTER LEAVING THE TOILET
bullets: Leave with the right foot first.
Say Ghufrānak after leaving.

title: WUDU: BEFORE YOU START
bullets: Intend purification in the heart.
Say Bismillah before beginning.
Use clean purifying water and avoid waste.
note: In Hanafi fiqh, intention and Bismillah are Sunnah acts of wudu, not among its four fard acts.
source: Hanafi fiqh: Nur al-Idah / Maraqi al-Falah.

title: WUDU: HANDS, MOUTH, NOSE
bullets: Wash both hands to the wrists three times.
Rinse the mouth three times.
Take water into the nose three times and expel it.
Use the right hand to take water and the left hand to clean the nose.
source: Hanafi fiqh manuals on the Sunnahs of wudu.

title: WUDU: FACE + ARMS
bullets: Wash the whole face. Once is fard; three times is Sunnah.
Wash the right arm including the elbow. Once is fard; three times is Sunnah.
Wash the left arm including the elbow the same way.
Make sure water reaches the entire required area.

title: WUDU: HEAD, EARS + FEET
bullets: Wipe the head once with wet hands. Hanafi fard minimum: at least one quarter of the head.
Wiping the whole head once is Sunnah.
Wipe the ears once.
Wash each foot including the ankle. Once is fard; three times is Sunnah.
Ensure water reaches between the toes and around the heels.

title: WUDU: THE 4 FARD ACTS
bullets: Wash the entire face once.
Wash both arms including the elbows once.
Wipe at least one quarter of the head once.
Wash both feet including the ankles once.
alert: IF ONE OF THESE IS MISSING, HANAFI WUDU IS NOT VALID.
source: Hanafi fiqh: Nur al-Idah / Maraqi al-Falah.

title: WHAT BREAKS WUDU
bullets: Anything exiting from the front or back private passages, including urine, stool, wind, sexual fluids, or blood from those passages.
Flowing blood, pus, or similar discharge that reaches beyond its point of exit.
Vomiting a mouthful.
Sleeping in a posture that does not firmly keep the buttocks seated; fainting, insanity, or intoxication.
Loud laughter by an adult inside a prayer containing ruku and sujud breaks both the prayer and wudu in Hanafi fiqh.
source: Hanafi fiqh: Nur al-Idah / Maraqi al-Falah.

title: DOUBT ABOUT WUDU
bullets: If you are certain you had wudu and only doubt whether it broke, you still have wudu.
If you are certain wudu broke and only doubt whether you renewed it, treat yourself as without wudu.
Certainty is not removed by mere doubt.
source: General Hanafi legal principle: certainty is not removed by doubt.
reflection_source: Classical Islamic legal maxim (al-yaqin la yazulu bi-l-shakk).

title: AFTER WUDU
arabic:
أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي مِنَ التَّوَّابِينَ، وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنَ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ
translit: Ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, wa ashhadu anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa rasūluh. Allāhumma-jʿalnī mina t-tawwābīn, wa-jʿalnī mina l-mutaṭahhirīn.
meaning: I testify that none is worthy of worship except Allah alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. O Allah, make me among those who repent and those who purify themselves.

title: TWO RAKʿAHS AFTER WUDU
bullets: After completing wudu, you may pray two voluntary rakʿahs.
Pray them with presence and concentration.
Do not begin them during a prohibited or restricted nafl time.
source: Hadith of Bilal: Sahih al-Bukhari 1149; Sahih Muslim 2458.
reflection: Bilal (may Allah be pleased with him) told the Prophet that whenever he made wudu, he prayed what Allah enabled him to pray afterward.

title: WHEN GHUSL BECOMES FARD
bullets: Ejaculation or sexual discharge meeting the conditions that require ghusl.
Sexual intercourse involving penetration, even without ejaculation.
The end of menstruation.
The end of post-natal bleeding.
source: Hanafi fiqh: standard causes of obligatory ghusl.

title: GHUSL: BARE MINIMUM
bullets: Rinse the entire mouth once.
Rinse the nose once so water reaches the soft area.
Wash the entire outer body once, ensuring water reaches all skin, hair roots, folds, and hidden outer areas.
alert: MISSING ANY ONE OF THESE LEAVES THE REQUIRED HANAFI GHUSL INCOMPLETE.
source: Hanafi fiqh: Nur al-Idah / Maraqi al-Falah.

title: GHUSL: FULL SUNNAH METHOD
bullets: Intend purification. Say Bismillah before uncovering if appropriate.
Wash the hands, private parts, and any physical impurity.
Perform a complete wudu. If water pools around the feet, wash the feet at the end.
Wash the head, then the right side, then the left, ensuring the whole body is reached.
The full Sunnah method includes thoroughly washing the body three times.
note: No special prayer recital is required while performing ghusl.
source: Hanafi fiqh; SeekersGuidance: ritual bath in Hanafi fiqh.

title: TAYAMMUM: WHEN ALLOWED
bullets: When sufficient water is genuinely unavailable after a reasonable search.
When using water would cause real harm, worsen illness, or significantly delay recovery.
When extreme cold creates a genuine danger and water cannot reasonably be warmed.
Simply disliking water or not wanting to get wet is not enough.

title: TAYAMMUM: HOW TO DO IT
bullets: Intend purification for worship.
Strike or place both hands on clean earth or an earth-derived surface, then wipe the entire face.
Strike/place the hands again, then wipe both arms including the elbows.
Tayammum ends when its excuse ends or by anything that breaks wudu.

title: ENTERING THE MASJID
meaning: O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.
bullets: Enter with the right foot first.
Say the duʿā as you enter.

title: TAHIYYAT AL-MASJID
bullets: When entering a masjid, pray two voluntary rakʿahs before sitting if prayer is permitted at that time.
If the obligatory congregation has begun, join it instead.
In Hanafi practice, once the Jumuʿah khutbah has begun, sit and listen rather than start a voluntary prayer.

title: LEAVING THE MASJID
meaning: O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty.
bullets: Leave with the left foot first.
Say the duʿā as you leave.

title: WHEN YOU HEAR THE ADHAN
arabic: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
translit: Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
meaning: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
bullets: Repeat the muʾadhdhin’s words.
At Ḥayya ʿala ṣ-ṣalāh and Ḥayya ʿala l-falāḥ, say the phrase above instead.
After the adhan, send blessings upon the Prophet ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam and then make the next card’s duʿā.
